name: Profhilo / skin booster injectables

lead: Profhilo and similar skin boosters are injected to make skin look more hydrated, supple and smooth, improving skin quality rather than adding volume the way a filler does. They are often positioned as a complement to fillers.

Profhilo, made by IBSA and sold in Europe since 2015, combines high and low molecular weight hyaluronic acid, which is proposed to hydrate the dermis and stimulate fibroblasts to make collagen and elastin. Small open-label studies and post-marketing data report gains in hydration and elasticity.

paras: It is injected into the skin by a clinician, in a short series of sessions. The skin-booster category covers products placed in the dermis for hydration, elasticity and texture. Many people combine it with filler or other skin treatments.

Reported effects are mostly minor swelling, redness and bruising. Hyaluronic acid injectables can rarely cause vascular occlusion. One source states Profhilo was not FDA-approved in the US as of January 2026.

angle.text: Profhilo and similar skin boosters are used to give a more hydrated, supple and smoother-looking complexion rather than added volume. Hyaluronic acid injected into the skin helps it hold more water, improving hydration and elasticity. Small studies report these gains.

lead: Profhilo is an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) product made by IBSA Derma, launched in Europe in 2015, that is marketed as a skin 'bio-remodelling' treatment rather than a volume filler.[1][2] Each syringe combines high and low molecular weight HA stabilised by a heat process, with no chemical cross-linker.[1]

The way it is meant to improve looks is through skin quality: smoother, better-hydrated, firmer-looking skin on the face, neck, hands and body, rather than the added bulk of a cheek or lip filler. Practitioners describe the chain as hydration and tissue remodelling, then improved elasticity and texture, then a fresher, less crepey appearance.

It belongs to a broader category called skin boosters: injectables placed in the dermis to improve hydration, elasticity and texture instead of adding volume. A 2024 review traces how the term evolved from HA fillers and notes that definitions of the category vary.[3]
Evidence consists mainly of small open-label studies and post-marketing data. As of January 2026, one source states that Profhilo was not FDA-approved in the US.[1]
infobox: High and low molecular weight hyaluronic acid, non-cross-linked[1]
CE-marked device in EU; not FDA-approved as of January 2026 per source[1]

paras: Each 2 ml syringe is reported to hold 64 mg of HA, half high molecular weight and half low, combined by IBSA's patented NAHYCO process.[1] Proponents describe 'hybrid cooperative complexes' that they say activate cellular processes in skin, a concept examined in a 2016 laboratory paper.[4] The product is used on the face, neck and body, and a typical course is described as two sessions about 30 days apart followed by maintenance.[1]
Skin boosters as a class include HA, polynucleotides and other materials, and reviews discuss their types and mechanisms.[3][5]

Profhilo is used on the face, neck, chest, hands and body to address skin laxity, roughness and fine wrinkles, and is often grouped with other skin boosters [1][6]. A 2025 review of non-facial rejuvenation of the neck, chest and hands covers injectable options including this kind of product [6].

Practitioners combine it with other treatments. A randomised trial in neck rejuvenation compared botulinum toxin alone with botulinum toxin followed by Profhilo gel [7], and a split-face randomised trial added Profhilo mesogel to subcision for atrophic acne scars [8].

Profhilo Body is a variant for the body, and Profhilo Structura is a higher-concentration formulation with 45 mg of total hyaluronic acid developed to restore facial adipose tissue, with a practical review focused on the superficial medial and lateral-temporal cheek fat compartments [9]. An initial case series in 22 volunteers aged 36 to 60 used Profhilo Structura in superficial fat of each hemiface [10].

Profhilo is delivered as small intradermal and superficial injections rather than deep depot placement. One reference page describes a standard facial course of two sessions about 30 days apart, followed by maintenance sessions at intervals of around two months, with each visit lasting roughly 15 to 30 minutes and performed by a licensed practitioner. [1] The same source describes a small number of injection points on each side of the face, placed with fine needles according to a mapped pattern, and notes that topical anaesthetic is optional. [1] IBSA names its placement pattern the Bio-Aesthetic Points technique. [1]

Because the gel is spread by the tissue rather than moulded into shape, practitioners describe the visible result as gradual skin change rather than an immediate contour change. Reported after-effects are redness, swelling, bruising, tenderness and itching at the injection points, which the same source says generally settle within a day or two. [1] Reference pages list hypersensitivity to hyaluronic acid, bleeding disorders and active infection or inflammation at the site among reasons treatment is deferred or avoided. [1]

Small open-label studies of roughly 11 to 64 participants report gains in hydration, elasticity and wrinkle scores lasting up to about six months, according to one source.[1] An expert panel consensus on stabilised HA skin boosters has also been published, and reviews evaluate the evidence for the category as mixed in quality.[5][11]

A 2026 systematic review of nine studies and 278 participants of Profhilo and Profhilo Body reported statistically significant changes or trends toward improvement in viscoelasticity, elasticity, hydration, density and laxity at sites including the malar and submalar face, neck, inner arms, abdomen, hands and knees, and improvements in the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale and Facial Volume Loss Scale [12].

IBSA is a Swiss pharmaceutical company founded in Lugano in 1945, and its IBSA Derma division introduced Profhilo, built on its NAHYCO stabilisation technology, in Europe in 2015 with CE marking. [1] Post-marketing safety reporting on tens of thousands of treated patients followed in the next few years, and the 2020 safety assessment of the high and low molecular weight hyaluronan combination summarises that experience. [2][2] A 2025 update describes nearly ten years of surveillance. [13]

Regulatory status differs by region. In Europe it is sold as a CE-marked medical device, and one reference page lists it on the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods since April 2022 and describes a China registration process begun after a distribution partnership announced in 2023. [1] The same page states that it had not been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration as of January 2026, and US studies are registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. [1] That page itself carries a note that some figures in its text are inconsistent, so dates and counts should be read as approximate.

A worldwide post-marketing safety assessment of Profhilo, on the market since 2015, covers tens of thousands of patients.[2] One source reports that most events were minor and transient, such as swelling, redness and bruising.[1] HA injectables generally carry risks of bruising, nodules and, rarely, vascular occlusion.[14]
A 2025 update on post-marketing surveillance data nearing ten years of use of hyaluronic acid hybrid cooperative complexes assessed safety [13].

Registered Profhilo studies include a trial in malar and sub-malar volume deficiency (n=64), neck (n=25), inner arm and abdomen (n=24), back of the hands (n=51), and Profhilo Structura (n=164).[15][16][17][18][19] A 2024 single-arm pilot study evaluated intradermal HA as a skin quality booster.[20]

A 2024 split-face randomised trial in 12 patients with atrophic acne scars compared subcision alone with subcision plus Profhilo, assessing scars by sonographic depth, blinded photographic ratings and patient satisfaction, and reported higher patient satisfaction scores on the Profhilo side [8]. A 2026 triple-blind split-face trial in 12 women aged 45 to 65 compared Profhilo with saline in the perioral region, using stereophotogrammetry, ultrasound, photographs and a Face-Q questionnaire at 60 days [21]. In the neck rejuvenation trial, 19 participants per group were evaluated three months after treatment using the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale and skin biophysical measures [7].
